applicant_utility.summary: The award is a one-time cut to tuition fees for the first year only, worth between EUR 2,000 and EUR 5,000 depending on your region, so you still need a funding plan for living costs in Dublin and for the remainder of your programme. Check the exemptions before you invest effort: business, engineering, natural sciences, computer science and statistics courses are excluded, and applicants from China are directed to the Claddagh Scholarship instead. Because everything is processed on a rolling basis, applying early in the next cycle matters more than polishing the application for months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU fee status international students holding an offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity outside the exempt subject areas (excluding China).
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your course is not in an exempt area: business, engineering, natural sciences, or computer science and statistics
Confirm you are not applying from China, in which case the Claddagh Scholarship applies instead
Have your full-time postgraduate taught course offer in hand before the regional closing date
Draft the statement on how you will contribute to the Trinity College Dublin community in advance
Submit the online form early, since assessment and awards are made on a rolling basis
Plan to fully accept the course offer once the award is communicated
common_rejection_risks: Applying to an exempt course area without noticing the exclusion list
Chinese applicants using this form instead of the Claddagh Scholarship
Applying without a course offer, since a course offer is part of the eligibility
Missing the regional closing date, which differs by up to three months between regions
Assuming the award renews into later years - it applies to the first year only
Expecting living-cost or travel support, which this scholarship does not provide
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Dublin and the remainder of the programme's tuition fees, since the award is a one-time reduction of at most EUR 5,000 applied to the first year only.
document_audit: The form itself is light - personal information plus a short statement - so the course offer carries the eligibility weight
If the online form is inaccessible in your region, the Trinity Regional Manager or Advisor can supply an alternative application form, so contact them early
alerts: The four 2026/2027 regional deadlines (1 April, 1 May, 15 June and 15 July 2026) have all passed, so the earliest realistic next window is the following intake; early application is advised because assessment is rolling
The award value is region-dependent, so the same profile can attract EUR 2,000 or EUR 5,000
Separate scholarship programmes exist for the exempt areas, so check the postgraduate scholarships overview for your subject
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online scholarship form before your regional closing date, then fully accept the course offer; questions go through the online course enquiry team.

official.deadline_note: The 2026 call closed with an applicant deadline of 23 October 2025, 16:00 Irish local time; the supervisor/mentor deadline was 6 November 2025, the research office endorsement deadline 13 November 2025, the call outcome was communicated at the end of April 2026 and awards started 1 September 2026. No next-call date is published.
official.status_note: The programme page is marked as closed for the 2026 call, and its important dates list shows every 2026 milestone (applicant deadline, supervisor deadline, research office deadline, call outcome and start date) as achieved.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award includes a contribution to fees, including non-EU fees, up to a maximum of EUR 5,750 per annum. Non-EU nationals may request an additional EUR 4,000 per annum above the standard fee contribution, and any remaining differential in fees must be paid by the grant recipient and/or the research body.

official.description: The Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme awards individual, prestigious research scholarships worth up to EUR 34,000 per annum - a stipend of EUR 25,000, a contribution to fees including non-EU fees of up to EUR 5,750, and eligible direct costs of EUR 3,250 - for a period of 1-4 years, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science and managed by Research Ireland.

verification.notes: The EUR 25,000 stipend, the EUR 5,750 fee contribution including non-EU fees with the additional EUR 4,000 for non-EU nationals, the EUR 3,250 direct costs, the EUR 34,000 annual maximum, the 1-4 year duration, the 18 percent success rate, the primary-supervisor rule of one applicant, the new-entrant eligibility change effective from the 2026 call and the 2026 call timeline (deadline 23 October 2025 16:00 Irish local time, outcome end of April 2026, start 1 September 2026) were confirmed on Research Ireland's official programme page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a large, highly competitive award (about 18 percent success over the past five years) rather than a guaranteed top-up, so apply with a genuinely pioneering, interdisciplinary bottom-up proposal and a supervisor who is not already primary supervisor for someone else in the same call. Cash-out depends on the year: the stipend is EUR 25,000, fees attract up to EUR 5,750 (or EUR 9,750 for non-EU nationals) and eligible direct costs EUR 3,250, giving the EUR 34,000 ceiling, but any remaining non-EU fee differential lands on you or your host research body. Note the new-entrant rule in force from the 2026 call: you must be newly entering the degree or in your first registered year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New entrants to a Master's or first-year PhD candidates with an exceptional research idea, a free primary supervisor and a research office that can endorse on time.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the new-entrant rule: new entry to the Master's or PhD, or first registered year of that degree, for the 2026 call onwards
Confirm your intended primary supervisor has no other applicant in the same call
Diarise the two-stage endorsement chain: supervisor/mentor deadline, then research office deadline, which come after the applicant deadline in the 2026 cycle
Budget the non-EU fee differential if applicable, since only part of it can be requested
Frame the proposal as bottom-up and non-directed, and flag pioneering or interdisciplinary elements explicitly
Plan for a spring outcome - the 2026 call outcome only came at the end of April, with awards starting 1 September
common_rejection_risks: Choosing a primary supervisor already supervising another applicant in the call
Missing the applicant deadline at 16:00 Irish local time or the later endorsement deadlines
Being beyond the first registered year of the target degree under the 2026 rule change
Proposing work within the remit of a strategic funding partner (EPA, DCEDIY, DFA or Met Éireann), which is directed rather than bottom-up
Assuming the EUR 34,000 covers all non-EU fees, when the remaining differential is payable by the recipient or research body
Relying on the award to start study expenses early, given the April outcome and September start
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any fee differential beyond the EUR 5,750 standard (plus the additional EUR 4,000 for non-EU nationals) fee contribution, and personal living costs above the EUR 25,000 stipend.
document_audit: The application is submitted online through the Research Ireland system, but the endorsements are separate submitted components, so start the chain early
Download the call document from the programme page for the definitive document list rather than relying on the summary
The programme is competitive and peer-reviewed internationally, so the proposal quality, not the form, is decisive
